$comment: What may leave the tenant inside a shareable export, and in what form.
This is an allowlist. A section that is not listed here is not exported, and
within a listed section a field that is not listed is not copied. Nothing is
removed by pattern matching, so a new analysis field added upstream is absent
by default rather than shipped by accident.
full      - one record per finding, ids and all
aggregate - counts only, no per-object ids
The dividing line for findings is what the record is about. A finding about a
Conditional Access policy is what the reviewer plans against, and its ids are
policy references that mean nothing outside the tenant. A finding about a
person is different: 2,646 records naming which individuals cannot perform MFA
is a ranked target list, and it tells a planner nothing that the single number
does not. Person-scoped checks are therefore aggregated, and anything not

droppedFields.$comment: Listed only to record why they are absent; the allowlist is what actually excludes them.
droppedFields.displayName: Masked to the object id anyway, so it carries no information the id does not, and keeping the key invites a future writer to populate it.
droppedFields.description: Per-instance generated prose. For person-scoped checks it interpolates a per-person alias token, which is the target list this classification exists to prevent.
droppedFields.summary: Per-instance generated prose. The static catalogue text in logic, threat and remediation carries the same meaning without interpolation.
droppedFields.topRisk: Derived from the full finding list including the aggregated ones, so it would reintroduce a person-scoped record through the summary.
